name: premium-explorer
description: Tell your projects apart at a glance: color-code folders in the Explorer. Git repos get a color automatically, or style any folder yourself.

commands.title: Premium Explorer: Disable Background Painting (Restore Workbench)

premiumExplorer.enabled.description: Color folders that contain a Git repository.

premiumExplorer.rules.markdownDescription:
Path-scoped coloring rules, evaluated by path specificity (a deeper rule wins). With no rules, nothing is colored.

- `git`: every Git repository under `path` is colored automatically, each from `premiumExplorer.palette`.
- `manual` (used when `engine` is omitted): the folder at `path` **and everything inside it** is styled by this rule's layer settings. A layer paints only when a `*Color` names one (per rule or globally) — a bare rule paints nothing.

Each folder is painted with independent layers — **background**, **edge** bar, **pill**, **text** and **watermark** watermark — set globally via `premiumExplorer.root*`/`premiumExplorer.inner*` and overridable per rule with the same `root*`/`inner*` keys (a `*Color` left empty falls back to the folder base).

Paths may be workspace-relative (`.`, `./projects`) or absolute.

```jsonc
"premiumExplorer.rules": [
  { "path": ".", "engine": "git" },
  { "path": "./notes", "rootBackgroundColor": "#00b8ff", "rootPill": "solid",
    "rootTextStyle": "bold", "innerBackgroundStyle": "none" },
  { "path": "./scratch" }
]
```

enumDescriptions: Auto-color every Git repository found under this path, each from `premiumExplorer.palette`.
Style this folder and everything inside it with the layer settings on this rule.
engine.markdownDescription: How this path is colored. Defaults to `manual` if omitted. (`default` is still accepted as an old name for `manual`.)

enumDescriptions: The folder's rendered block reads as one plate: the root row takes the top corners, the last row rendered under it the bottom ones, everything between stays square.
Every row rounds its own box, giving a stack of separately rounded bars.
radiusScale.markdownDescription: What this folder's corner radii are rounded around — its whole rendered block (the default) or each row on its own. Overrides `premiumExplorer.radiusScale`.

enumDescriptions: No full-row fill — bare VS Code styling.
Fill the whole row with the background color.
Reuse whatever the nearest **enclosing** colored folder paints on its inner rows (blend into the parent instead of punching a hole in it).
rootBackgroundStyle.markdownDescription: **Background** layer for the repo root row. `none` = not painted, `solid` = this rule's color, `inherit` = the enclosing colored folder's inner look.

rootBackgroundColor.markdownDescription: Color of the full-row fill for the repo root row. Empty falls back to the repo's hashed palette color for a `git` rule; a `manual` rule with no color here leaves this layer unpainted.

alpha.description: The stop’s own alpha (0–1). Multiplies on any alpha the hex itself carries.

at.description: Position 0–100 (%). In a split fill, where this band ends.

stops.description: The colour stops, in order. A bare hex is an opaque stop.

blend.description: split = hard edges between the colours; gradient = blended (the default).

direction.description: Where the fill runs; a number is a CSS gradient angle in degrees. Default horizontal (left → right).

rootBackgroundFill.markdownDescription: Multi-stop fill for the repo root row’s background — the shared Fill type (docs/fill-spec.md): a hex, or `{stops, blend?, direction?}` with each stop a hex or `{color, alpha?, at?}`. Wins over `rootBackgroundColor`; applies only while `rootBackgroundStyle` is `solid`. `rootBackgroundOpacity` multiplies on each stop’s alpha, so an alpha-0 stop stays transparent and the theme shows through. A multi-stop fill is painted as a background image, so it does not brighten on hover (a solid fill still does).

enumDescriptions: Block for any direction with a vertical component, row for a purely horizontal one — so a diagonal or vertical fill is visible without having to know this key exists.
Every row paints the whole fill inside its own ~22px box. The only scale a horizontal fill needs.
One fill stretched over the folder's rendered block, each row showing the slice that belongs at its depth.
rootBackgroundFillScale.markdownDescription:
How far the multi-stop fill on the repo root row is stretched.

A CSS gradient splits its colour change between the two axes in proportion to the box it fills, and a row is about 300 x 22 px — so inside one row a diagonal has only ~7% of its change left on the vertical axis, which is why `"diagonal"` used to look exactly like `"horizontal"`, and why `"vertical"` repeated its whole fade inside every row. Stretched over a 20-row block a diagonal puts ~60% there and reads as a diagonal.

Only applies to `#premiumExplorer.rootBackgroundFill#` when it resolves to a gradient; a flat colour has nothing to stretch. While the folder is partly scrolled out the block is the *rendered* extent, so the fill's ends drift.

rootPillOpacity.markdownDescription: Opacity of the pill for the repo root row.

rootPillRadius.markdownDescription: Corner radius for the pill on the repo root row. A number rounds all four corners; the per-corner form takes the CSS order *top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left*, as a short array (`[6, 6, 0, 0]`) or a string (`"6 6 0 0"`), filling in fewer entries exactly as the CSS `border-radius` shorthand does.

rootPillPadding.markdownDescription:
Space the pill leaves around the label on the repo root row, in px.

```jsonc
5                 // horizontal only — vertical stays 0 (what ships today)
[2, 8]            // vertical, horizontal
[2, 8, 2, 6]      // CSS order: top right bottom left
```

**A single number is horizontal only**, which is not what CSS `padding: 5px` means. That is deliberate: the shipped pill is `0 5px`, so `5` has to keep reproducing it. Two, three and four values follow the CSS shorthand exactly.

**Vertical padding is the risky axis.** A row is about 22px and the label's line box already fills most of it, so vertical padding grows the pill past the row: it will overlap the rows above and below rather than being clipped. 0–2 is usually as far as it goes. The corner radius needs no adjusting — the browser clamps `border-radius` to half the final box, padding included.

rootBackgroundRadius.markdownDescription:
Corner radius for the full-row fill on the repo root row. A number rounds all four corners; the per-corner form takes the CSS order *top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left*, as a short array (`[6, 6, 0, 0]`) or a string (`"6 6 0 0"`), filling in fewer entries exactly as the CSS `border-radius` shorthand does.

Applied as a `border-radius` on the row, which clips **every** background layer at once — fill, edge bar and watermark — so it rounds the whole painted plate. The row's text is never clipped. `#premiumExplorer.radiusScale#` decides whether the rounding is per row or around the folder's block.

rootEdgeRadius.markdownDescription:
Corner radius for the edge bar on the repo root row. A number rounds all four corners; the per-corner form takes the CSS order *top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left*, as a short array (`[6, 6, 0, 0]`) or a string (`"6 6 0 0"`), filling in fewer entries exactly as the CSS `border-radius` shorthand does.

The bar is a background *image*, and an image cannot carry a radius of its own, so this rounds the row's **left** corners — exactly the two the bar occupies — and takes whichever of this and `#premiumExplorer.rootBackgroundRadius#` is larger there. An inset *capsule* bar (all four corners, floating clear of the row edges) would need its own element in the row and is deliberately not offered.

rootTextStyle.markdownDescription: **Text** weight/style for the repo root row's label.
enumDescriptions: No weight/style change — the theme decides.

rootTextColor.markdownDescription: Label text color for the repo root row. Empty = leave it to the theme.

rootMark.markdownDescription:
A single fixed glyph stamped just after the label on the repo root row — a per-folder mark, at full size and in its own colours, rather than the faint tiled watermark.

- A **built-in glyph**: `ansible`, `argo`, `claude`, `docker`, `fluxcd`, `git`, `kubernetes`, `pulumi`, `terraform`.
- A **character or emoji**: `🐳`, `⚙` (drawn in `markColor`, or the theme foreground).
- A **path to an `.svg` file**, inline `<svg>` markup, or a `data:image/svg+xml` URI — resolved exactly like `#premiumExplorer.backgroundWatermarkSymbol#`.

It does **not** compete with Git's status letter: that one lives in VS Code's single file-decoration badge slot, while the mark is painted by the injected CSS, so both show at once. (`#premiumExplorer.badge#` does take that slot, and does hide the letter.) Empty = no mark.

rootMarkColor.markdownDescription: Tint for `#premiumExplorer.rootMark#`. Empty keeps an SVG's own colours — which is usually the point of picking a real logo. A character mark needs one, and falls back to the theme foreground.

rootMarkGap.markdownDescription: Gap (px) between the end of the row's text and `#premiumExplorer.rootMark#`.

rootMarkInPill.markdownDescription:
Grow the pill on the repo root row rightwards so it **encloses the mark**, instead of letting the mark sit just outside the plate.

The pill gains `markGap + markSize + 5px` of right padding and the mark stays anchored to the text, so the rounded plate wraps label and mark together. A no-op where either the pill or the mark is off.

Two things to expect: a pill fill that fades to alpha 0 at its right end fades across the **wider** box, so an enclosed mark may sit on nothing — use a fill that still has colour at its right edge. And hover brightens the pill (`--fc-pill-hover`) but not the mark, so an enclosed mark does not brighten with its plate.

rootEdgeWidth.markdownDescription: Width in px of the repo root row's edge bar.

rootEdgeStripeSize.markdownDescription: Thickness in px of one diagonal stripe band on the repo root row's edge bar.

rootEdgeDirection.markdownDescription: Where the repo root row's edge stripe runs. `diagonal-reverse` is the classic 45° stripe (bottom-left → top-right); `diagonal` slants the other way; `vertical` runs top → bottom (horizontally stacked bands); `horizontal` runs left → right. A number is a CSS gradient angle in degrees.

enumDescriptions: Hard-edged bands — the classic striped bar.
The colour sequence blended smoothly into each other.

rootWatermarkStyle.markdownDescription: **Watermark** layer for the repo root row: artwork scattered faintly behind the row (the rule's `backgroundWatermarkSymbol`, else the folder name's initial).

rootWatermarkColor.markdownDescription: Watermark color for the repo root row. Empty = **the row's own fill colour**, stepped just clear of the row so the pattern reads as texture in the background rather than a colour laid over it — how far is `rootWatermarkContrast`. Set `original` to keep a custom SVG's own colors instead of flattening it to one shade.

rootWatermarkContrast.markdownDescription: How far the watermark on the repo root row steps off the fill colour it inherits, as a fraction of the distance to white (over a dark row) or black (over a light one). The step is what lifts the pattern clear of the row it paints on; keep it small so the watermarks stay a shade of the background rather than a colour of their own. Ignored once `rootWatermarkColor` pins a color. 0 = the fill colour exactly, 0.5 = a washed-out mark.

enumDescriptions: Both. The clearing does the general work and breaks the pattern up so no two folders look alike; the text cover then catches whatever a long name still runs into, which a clearing fixed to the canvas cannot know about.
Only the text cover: every copy a row's own text reaches is dimmed whole — never clipped half way — and the rest of the scatter is left even.
Only the baked clearing: fewer and fainter copies down the middle of the canvas where names run, full strength out in the margins. Costs nothing at paint time and never touches the row's colour.
rootWatermarkDimStyle.markdownDescription: How the watermark on the repo root row gets out of the way of what you are reading.

enumDescriptions: The jittered field across the whole canvas.
The same field squeezed into a band at the right edge, so the glyphs hug the far side and keep clear of the filenames.
One horizontal line of glyphs in the canvas's top band, laid out from the right edge.
A single oversized glyph hugging the top-right corner, read as a badge. One per canvas; `watermarkDensity`, `watermarkVariation` and `watermarkRotation` have nothing to vary.
rootWatermarkLayout.markdownDescription:
How the watermark copies are arranged on the repo root row's canvas.

With `row`, the canvas left at its default puts that one line on the folder's root row and nowhere else; setting `watermarkCanvas` to a row's height (22) repeats it once per row instead.

For *"every glyph a name reaches drops to ~7%"*, set `watermarkDimStyle` to `text` and `watermarkDim` to `0.93` — the cover takes back `dim` of each copy's own opacity, so what is left is `1 - dim`.

rootWatermarkDim.markdownDescription: How far the watermark is dimmed on the repo root row, as a fraction. It sets the strength of whichever dimming `rootWatermarkDimStyle` selects: how much thinner and fainter the scatter gets down the middle of the canvas, and how far a copy the row's text runs into is taken back. `0` turns dimming off entirely.

rootWatermarkOpacity.markdownDescription: Opacity of the repo root row's watermark. Keep it low — it should read as texture, not content.

rootWatermarkSize.markdownDescription: Watermark size in px for the repo root row — the average, since individual copies vary by `rootWatermarkVariation`. The canvas is 512px, so this can go a lot larger than a text watermark normally would.

Space the pill leaves around the label on the repo root row, in px.

```jsonc
5                 // horizontal only — vertical stays 0 (what ships today)
[2, 8]            // vertical, horizontal
[2, 8, 2, 6]      // CSS order: top right bottom left
```

**A single number is horizontal only**, which is not what CSS `padding: 5px` means. That is deliberate: the shipped pill is `0 5px`, so `5` has to keep reproducing it. Two, three and four values follow the CSS shorthand exactly.

premiumExplorer.innerEdgeWidth.markdownDescription: Width in px of the inner rows (files/folders inside)'s edge bar.

premiumExplorer.innerEdgeStripeSize.markdownDescription: Thickness in px of one diagonal stripe band on the inner rows (files/folders inside)'s edge bar.

premiumExplorer.innerEdgeDirection.markdownDescription: Where the inner rows (files/folders inside)'s edge stripe runs. `diagonal-reverse` is the classic 45° stripe (bottom-left → top-right); `diagonal` slants the other way; `vertical` runs top → bottom (horizontally stacked bands); `horizontal` runs left → right. A number is a CSS gradient angle in degrees.

enumDescriptions: Hard-edged bands — the classic striped bar.
The colour sequence blended smoothly into each other.
premiumExplorer.innerEdgeBlend.markdownDescription: How the inner rows (files/folders inside)'s edge colours are drawn: hard-edged bands, or the sequence blended into a gradient. Band thickness stays `#premiumExplorer.innerEdgeStripeSize#` either way.

enumDescriptions: No watermark — bare VS Code styling.
Scatter the folder's watermark faintly behind the row.
Reuse whatever the nearest **enclosing** colored folder paints on its inner rows.
premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkStyle.markdownDescription: **Watermark** layer for the inner rows (files/folders inside): a faint tiled watermark behind the row (the rule's `backgroundWatermarkSymbol`, else the folder name's initial).

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkColor.markdownDescription: Watermark color for the rows inside a colored folder. Empty = **the row's own fill colour**, stepped just clear of the row so the pattern reads as texture in the background rather than a colour laid over it — how far is `#premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkContrast#`. Set `original` to keep a custom SVG's own colors instead of flattening it to one shade.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkContrast.markdownDescription: How far the watermark on the rows inside a colored folder steps off the fill colour it inherits, as a fraction of the distance to white (over a dark row) or black (over a light one). The step is what lifts the pattern clear of the row it paints on; keep it small so the watermarks stay a shade of the background rather than a colour of their own. Ignored once `#premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkColor#` pins a color. 0 = the fill colour exactly, 0.5 = a washed-out mark.

enumDescriptions: Both. The clearing does the general work and breaks the pattern up so no two folders look alike; the text cover then catches whatever a long name still runs into, which a clearing fixed to the canvas cannot know about.
Only the text cover: every copy a row's own text reaches is dimmed whole — never clipped half way — and the rest of the scatter is left even.
Only the baked clearing: fewer and fainter copies down the middle of the canvas where names run, full strength out in the margins. Costs nothing at paint time and never touches the row's colour.
premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkDimStyle.markdownDescription: How the watermark on the rows inside a colored folder gets out of the way of what you are reading.

enumDescriptions: The jittered field across the whole canvas.
The same field squeezed into a band at the right edge, so the glyphs hug the far side and keep clear of the filenames.
One horizontal line of glyphs in the canvas's top band, laid out from the right edge.
A single oversized glyph hugging the top-right corner, read as a badge. One per canvas; `watermarkDensity`, `watermarkVariation` and `watermarkRotation` have nothing to vary.
premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkLayout.markdownDescription:
How the watermark copies are arranged on the inner rows' canvas.

With `row`, the canvas left at its default puts that one line on the folder's root row and nowhere else; setting `watermarkCanvas` to a row's height (22) repeats it once per row instead.

For *"every glyph a name reaches drops to ~7%"*, set `watermarkDimStyle` to `text` and `watermarkDim` to `0.93` — the cover takes back `dim` of each copy's own opacity, so what is left is `1 - dim`.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkDim.markdownDescription: How far the watermark is dimmed on the rows inside a colored folder, as a fraction. It sets the strength of whichever dimming `#premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkDimStyle#` selects: how much thinner and fainter the scatter gets down the middle of the canvas, and how far a copy the row's text runs into is taken back. `0` turns dimming off entirely.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkOpacity.markdownDescription: Opacity of the inner rows watermark. It paints over the row's fill, so this is how far the pattern darkens it.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkSize.markdownDescription: Watermark size in px for the rows inside a colored folder — the average, since individual copies vary by `innerWatermarkVariation`. The canvas is 512px, so this can go a lot larger than a text watermark normally would.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkCanvas.markdownDescription: Size in px of the square canvas the rows inside a colored folder watermark is drawn on. At the default 512 it is wider than any sidebar and ~23 rows tall, so the background reads as one unique composition instead of a repeating tile. Smaller values start to look like wallpaper.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkDensity.markdownDescription: Watermarks per 100x100px of canvas for the rows inside a colored folder. Higher packs them tighter; the count scales with `innerWatermarkCanvas` so resizing the canvas keeps the same look.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkVariation.markdownDescription: 0-1 — how much the rows inside a colored folder watermarks vary in size, brightness and position. 0 is a uniform grid; tilt is separate, see `innerWatermarkRotation`.

premiumExplorer.edgeColorCount.markdownDescription: How many colours an **auto-derived** edge sequence uses. `1` reproduces a plain single-colour bar. Ignored where `*EdgeColors` is set explicitly.

enumDescriptions: Hash the folder name, so folders with the same name share a color.
Hash the full folder path, so every folder gets an independent color.
premiumExplorer.colorBy.description: What to hash when picking an automatic color for a Git repository folder.

enumDescriptions: Leave it unpainted, even though a rule names it.
Paint it in its rule's color but dimmer, so it reads as a link rather than as the folder it points at.
Paint it exactly like a real folder — no way to tell them apart on screen.
premiumExplorer.symlinkFolders.markdownDescription: How a folder that is **itself a symlink** is painted when a rule names its path. Symlinks are otherwise never colored: a `git` rule does not descend into them while discovering repositories, so a repo is not found — and colored — twice under two different paths. A symlink *inside* a colored folder is still painted like any other row in that folder, and is not covered by this setting.

enumDescriptions: The filename, the status letter and the folder dot are lifted clear of the row, and the letter gets a plate stepped off the row's ground with a border in Git's own colour. Applied only where a background actually paints.
Exactly what VS Code does — the status colour untouched, whatever is under it.
The lift, with a border in the lifted hue and no plate.
The status colour becomes the letter’s plate, with the letter knocked out of it.
Hide the status letter and the folder dot; the filename still lifts.
premiumExplorer.gitMarkStyle.markdownDescription:
How Git's status marks are kept readable once Premium Explorer paints a background under them.

VS Code picks the status colour against the *theme's* background, so over a fill it can fall a long way short of readable — measured over an amber fill: modified 3.4:1, added 2.5:1, deleted 1.3:1, against a 4.5:1 target. `chip` fixes that by lifting each mark against the colour the row actually shows, and putting the letter on a plate stepped off that same ground with a border at Git's own hex.

`chip` applies to **every row of a coloured folder**, including the ones that paint no fill of their own: with `innerBackgroundStyle: none` the children sit on the theme's own ground, where three of Git's four hexes already pass and the lift is simply a no-op — but deleted still fails at 3.3:1 and is lifted even there. A row outside every coloured folder keeps exactly what VS Code painted; `bare` opts out everywhere.

**Selection outranks Git.** On a selected row the filename takes `#premiumExplorer.selectedTextColor#` and the status colour is dropped, because the plate and the border still carry which status it is — and the chip inverts to dark-on-light so the letter stays legible on a bright selection.

premiumExplorer.gitMarkContrast.markdownDescription: The WCAG contrast ratio an `auto` git-mark colour is lifted to, against the colour the row actually shows. 4.5:1 is the WCAG AA threshold for body text; 3:1 is the large-text threshold. A lift stops as soon as it reaches the target, so the mark keeps as much of its status colour as the target allows — and if the target is unreachable (a mid grey has no colour at 4.5:1) the mark lands as close as it can rather than vanishing.

premiumExplorer.gitLabelColor.markdownDescription:
The **filename** of a file Git has decorated.

- `auto` — derived in the browser from the colour the row *actually* shows, lifted until it reads at `#premiumExplorer.gitMarkContrast#`:1. This is the only value that can be right in every theme, over every fill.
- a **hex** — used as given.
- `off` — leave whatever VS Code painted alone.
- a **per-status map** — `{"modified": "#…", "deleted": "auto"}`; the four keys are `modified`, `added`, `untracked`, `deleted`. A decoration from some other extension gets the single/`auto` treatment, since it has no git status.

**Selection outranks this entirely**: on a selected row the filename takes `#premiumExplorer.selectedTextColor#` and the status colour is dropped, since the chip's plate and border still carry which status it is.

premiumExplorer.gitMarkColor.markdownDescription:
The **status letter**'s ink (`M`, `A`, `U`, `D`).

- `auto` — derived in the browser from the colour the row *actually* shows, lifted until it reads at `#premiumExplorer.gitMarkContrast#`:1. This is the only value that can be right in every theme, over every fill.
- a **hex** — used as given.
- `off` — leave whatever VS Code painted alone.
- a **per-status map** — `{"modified": "#…", "deleted": "auto"}`; the four keys are `modified`, `added`, `untracked`, `deleted`. A decoration from some other extension gets the single/`auto` treatment, since it has no git status.

premiumExplorer.gitMarkBackgroundColor.markdownDescription:
The **plate** behind the status letter, under `gitMarkStyle: chip` or `solid`.

- `auto` — derived in the browser from the colour the row *actually* shows, lifted until it reads at `#premiumExplorer.gitMarkContrast#`:1. This is the only value that can be right in every theme, over every fill.
- a **hex** — used as given.
- `off` — leave whatever VS Code painted alone.
- a **per-status map** — `{"modified": "#…", "deleted": "auto"}`; the four keys are `modified`, `added`, `untracked`, `deleted`. A decoration from some other extension gets the single/`auto` treatment, since it has no git status.

`auto` means the row's own ground stepped off itself for `chip`, and the status colour lifted until a knockout letter reads out of it for `solid`.

premiumExplorer.gitMarkBorderColor.markdownDescription:
The status letter's **border**.

- `auto` — derived in the browser from the colour the row *actually* shows, lifted until it reads at `#premiumExplorer.gitMarkContrast#`:1. This is the only value that can be right in every theme, over every fill.
- a **hex** — used as given.
- `off` — leave whatever VS Code painted alone.
- a **per-status map** — `{"modified": "#…", "deleted": "auto"}`; the four keys are `modified`, `added`, `untracked`, `deleted`. A decoration from some other extension gets the single/`auto` treatment, since it has no git status.

`auto` keeps Git's own hex for `chip` — the plate says *a mark*, the border says *which* mark — and takes the lifted hue for `outline`.

premiumExplorer.gitFolderDotColor.markdownDescription:
The **dot** on a folder that contains changes.

- `auto` — derived in the browser from the colour the row *actually* shows, lifted until it reads at `#premiumExplorer.gitMarkContrast#`:1. This is the only value that can be right in every theme, over every fill.
- a **hex** — used as given.
- `off` — leave whatever VS Code painted alone.
- a **per-status map** — `{"modified": "#…", "deleted": "auto"}`; the four keys are `modified`, `added`, `untracked`, `deleted`. A decoration from some other extension gets the single/`auto` treatment, since it has no git status.

VS Code draws it at 40% opacity, which would undo any lift, so a row we take over shows it at full strength with a halo in the plate colour.

premiumExplorer.symlinkMark.markdownDescription:
An **extra** mark Premium Explorer stamps beside the label of a folder that is itself a symlink and that one of your rules names by path. Empty (the default) = none, which is usually right: VS Code already marks a symlink with a `⤷` in the file-decoration badge, and `#premiumExplorer.symlinkMarkColor#` colours that one.

Set this only where the native arrow cannot be seen — VS Code drops it on a **compressed** row (`linked/nested` collapsed into one), and `#premiumExplorer.badge#` hides it by taking the badge slot. Setting it otherwise gives the row two arrows.

It takes the same sources as `#premiumExplorer.rootMark#` and needs `#premiumExplorer.symlinkFolders#` to be something other than `none`, or the folder is never painted at all.

premiumExplorer.symlinkMarkColor.markdownDescription:
The colour of the **symlink arrow** VS Code appends to a symlinked row's file-decoration badge (`⤷`).

- `auto` — the tree's own icon foreground, i.e. the chevron ink.
- a **hex** — used as given.
- `off` — leave whatever VS Code painted.

On a **selected** row it swaps for `#premiumExplorer.selectedTextColor#`, exactly as the Git letter does.

**It only applies where the arrow is the whole badge.** Beside a Git status letter the two arrive as one string (`U, ⤷`) in one `::after` with one colour, so there is nothing to colour separately and `#premiumExplorer.gitMarkStyle#` governs both — which is also what plates them together into one chip.

enumDescriptions: The folder's rendered block reads as one plate: the root row takes the top corners, the last row rendered under it the bottom ones, everything between stays square.
Every row rounds its own box, giving a stack of separately rounded bars.
premiumExplorer.radiusScale.markdownDescription:
What a corner radius is rounded **around**. Inert until one of the `*BackgroundRadius` / `*EdgeRadius` keys is actually set.

A coloured folder spans many rows, so rounding each one gives a stack of separate rounded bars; rounding the block is what reads as one plate. While a folder's end is scrolled out of view the bottom corners are left square rather than drawing a false end mid-folder.

premiumExplorer.badge.markdownDescription: Optional badge (max 2 characters) shown next to Git repository folders, e.g. `●`. Leave empty to color the label only.

premiumExplorer.palette.markdownDescription: Colors (hex) used to auto-assign a per-repo color by hashing its name/path. Up to 16 entries. Fewer entries = fewer distinct colors.

enumDescriptions: The color the row already shows, lifted a step away from the theme.
The color that row is filled with, at full strength.

premiumExplorer.selectedBackgroundColor.markdownDescription:
Background of the selected/focused Explorer row inside a colored folder.

- `shift` — whatever the row already shows, lifted a step (`#premiumExplorer.selectedShift#`), so the selection reads as *this row, marked* instead of a foreign highlight. Carries its own strength, so `#premiumExplorer.selectedOpacity#` does not apply: compositing a shift back over the color it was measured from would cancel it out.
- `invert` — the color that row is filled with (its `*BackgroundColor`, else the folder base), at `#premiumExplorer.selectedOpacity#`.
- A hex such as `#ffffff`, at `#premiumExplorer.selectedOpacity#`.

Applies only when `background` is listed in `#premiumExplorer.selectedOverrides#`.

alpha.description: The stop’s own alpha (0–1). Multiplies on any alpha the hex itself carries.

at.description: Position 0–100 (%). In a split fill, where this band ends.

stops.description: The colour stops, in order. A bare hex is an opaque stop.

blend.description: split = hard edges between the colours; gradient = blended (the default).

direction.description: Where the fill runs; a number is a CSS gradient angle in degrees. Default horizontal (left → right).

premiumExplorer.selectedBackgroundFill.markdownDescription: Multi-stop fill for the selected row — the shared Fill type (docs/fill-spec.md): a hex, or `{stops, blend?, direction?}` with each stop a hex or `{color, alpha?, at?}`. When set it wins over `#premiumExplorer.selectedBackgroundColor#` entirely; `#premiumExplorer.selectedOpacity#` multiplies on each stop’s alpha, `#premiumExplorer.selectedInactiveDarken#` darkens every stop while the Explorer is unfocused, and `#premiumExplorer.selectedBorder#` set to `auto` derives the ring from this fill (one step darker than its centre colour). Takes effect on the styles named in `#premiumExplorer.selectedOverrides#`, like every selection colour. Edited in settings.json (objects have no Settings-UI editor).

premiumExplorer.selectedShift.markdownDescription: How far `shift` lifts the selected row off the color it already shows, as a fraction of the distance to white on a dark theme (black on a light one). `0.05` is barely there; `0.12` reads clearly without losing the folder's color; `0.4` is close to a plain highlight. Only used when `#premiumExplorer.selectedBackgroundColor#` is `shift`; the Explorer shifts by less than half this while it is unfocused.

premiumExplorer.selectedTextColor.markdownDescription: Text color of the selected/focused row. `auto` = black or white chosen for contrast, or a hex.

premiumExplorer.selectedOpacity.markdownDescription: Opacity of the selected row background (1 = solid).

premiumExplorer.selectedBold.markdownDescription: Make the selected/focused row’s label bold.

premiumExplorer.selectedBorder.markdownDescription: Border (focus ring) drawn around the selected row **while the Explorer is focused**. `none` = no border, `auto` = the theme’s focus-outline color, or a hex.

premiumExplorer.selectedInactiveDarken.markdownDescription: How much darker the selected row becomes when the Explorer is **not** focused (0 = same color, 1 = black). The border is also dropped while unfocused, mirroring VS Code’s inactive selection.

enumDescriptions: The box gets out of the way: transparent field, the row's own fill and watermark carrying through, a border marking where the typing goes.
The box shows as a real inset text field in the theme's own input colours, over the shifted row.
`dim`, plus the edge bar switches to the theme focus accent for as long as the box is open.
premiumExplorer.selectedRenameStyle.markdownDescription:
How a row looks while its inline **rename** box is open, on top of the step the row itself takes off its usual colour.

`edge` is the one exception to the rule that the edge bar always keeps its own colours: it is opt-in, it lasts only while a rename is actually open, and renaming is the one state where saying *where the typing is* outranks saying which folder the row belongs to.

premiumExplorer.backgroundWatermarkSymbo.markdownDescription:
Default watermark artwork for every colored folder, tiled faintly behind the rows.

- A **built-in glyph** shipped with the extension: `ansible`, `argo`, `claude`, `docker`, `fluxcd`, `git`, `kubernetes`, `pulumi`, `terraform`.
- A **character or emoji**: `🐳`, `⚙`. Only the first two characters are drawn, so a longer word that is not a glyph name is almost certainly a typo.
- A **path to an `.svg` file**: `./.vscode/whale.svg`, `~/icons/aws.svg`. Relative paths resolve against the folder itself, then each workspace root, and a readable file wins over a built-in glyph of the same name. Inline `<svg>` markup and `data:image/svg+xml` URIs also work.

Empty = each folder uses the first letter of its own name. Whether it is *drawn* is up to `#premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkStyle#` / `#premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkStyle#`.

A **list** mixes drawings: every copy on the canvas picks one, seeded off the folder so the mix is stable (`["docker", "terraform"]`, or `["✦", "◇"]`).

premiumExplorer.backgroundWatermark.markdownDeprecationMessage: Renamed to `#premiumExplorer.backgroundWatermarkSymbol#`, which also takes the name of a glyph shipped with the extension. Still read while that one is unset.

premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkCanvas.markdownDescription: Size in px of the square canvas the repo root row watermark is drawn on. At the default 512 it is wider than any sidebar and ~23 rows tall, so the background reads as one unique composition instead of a repeating tile. Smaller values start to look like wallpaper.

premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkDensity.markdownDescription: Watermarks per 100x100px of canvas for the repo root row. Higher packs them tighter; the count scales with `rootWatermarkCanvas` so resizing the canvas keeps the same look.

premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkVariation.markdownDescription: 0-1 — how much the repo root row watermarks vary in size, brightness and position. 0 is a uniform grid; tilt is separate, see `rootWatermarkRotation`.

premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkRotation.markdownDescription: Max tilt in degrees for the repo root row watermarks; each copy is rotated somewhere within +/- this. Tilt is what keeps repeated copies of one mark from reading as a grid, so it stays useful even at `rootWatermarkVariation: 0`. 180 spins them any which way.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkRotation.markdownDescription: Max tilt in degrees for the rows inside a colored folder watermarks; each copy is rotated somewhere within +/- this. Tilt is what keeps repeated copies of one mark from reading as a grid, so it stays useful even at `innerWatermarkVariation: 0`. 180 spins them any which way.

enumDescriptions: Fill the row with `selectedBackgroundColor`.
Re-tint the watermark to `selectedWatermarkColor`.
Paint the label with `selectedTextColor`.
Fill the pill behind the label with the selection color.

premiumExplorer.selectedOverrides.markdownDescription:
Which styles the selection color takes over. **Only what is listed changes on a selected row** — everything else keeps painting exactly as it does unselected.

- `["background"]` — only the row fill turns the selection color; the watermark and label are untouched.
- `[]` — selection changes nothing but the focus ring (`selectedBorder`, which is always its own setting).
- Default `["background", "watermarks", "text-color"]` — the row is filled, the watermark is re-tinted to match, and the label takes `selectedTextColor`.

The **edge bar is never taken over**: it is the one mark that still says which folder a selected or renaming row belongs to, so it always keeps its own colours.

`pills` is out of the default: a pill the selection has not taken over keeps its own fill and gains a traced edge, so an `invert` highlight painting the row in the pill color does not swallow it.

premiumExplorer.selectedWatermarkColor.markdownDescription:
Watermark color on a selected row, when `watermarks` is in `#premiumExplorer.selectedOverrides#`.

- `auto` (default) — a shade just off the selection color: darker when the selection is light, lighter when it is dark. How far off is `#premiumExplorer.selectedWatermarkContrast#`.
- A hex — that exact color, whatever the selection is.

premiumExplorer.selectedWatermarkContras.markdownDescription:
How far the `auto` selected watermark sits off the color the row is actually painted, as a fraction of the distance to black or white. Only used when `#premiumExplorer.selectedWatermarkColor#` is `auto` and `watermarks` is in `#premiumExplorer.selectedOverrides#`.

The watermark's normal color is picked to read against the folder's own fill, so on a bright selection it lands far too dark. This pulls it back to just off the selection — present, but with no contrast to fight the label. `selectedOpacity` is accounted for, so the step is measured from what is on screen rather than the configured color.

- `0` — identical to the selection (invisible).
- `0.08` (default) — barely there.
- `0.4+` — an obvious pattern under the selection.

premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkDimWidth.markdownDescription: The width in px of that clearing on the repo root row. It is baked into the canvas, so resizing the Explorer cannot change how any watermark is drawn.

premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkDimHeight.markdownDescription: The height in px of the clearing on the repo root row — how far apart its points sit down the canvas. Capped at `#premiumExplorer.rootWatermarkCanvas#`, and the shape tapers to a point at top and bottom so it tiles seamlessly.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkDimWidth.markdownDescription: The width in px of that clearing on the rows inside a colored folder. It is baked into the canvas, so resizing the Explorer cannot change how any watermark is drawn.

premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkDimHeight.markdownDescription: The height in px of the clearing on the rows inside a colored folder — how far apart its points sit down the canvas. Capped at `#premiumExplorer.innerWatermarkCanvas#`, and the shape tapers to a point at top and bottom so it tiles seamlessly.

premiumExplorer.symlinkMarkTint.markdownDescription: Tint for `#premiumExplorer.symlinkMark#`, the mark Premium Explorer stamps itself. Empty keeps an SVG's own colours; a character mark falls back to the theme foreground. This is a different thing from `#premiumExplorer.symlinkMarkColor#`, which colours VS Code's own arrow in the badge.
